reports.title: Jefferson Capital Reports Third Quarter 2026 Results

desk.headline: Revenue up 23% to $185.5m, beat; record $318m of debt purchases; no guidance given
results: Collections rose 35% to a record $319.2m, and spending on new debt portfolios more than doubled to $318.0m, with triple-digit growth in the US, UK and Latin America.
Revenue grew 23% to $185.5m and net income rose 22% to $46.9m ($0.76 a share vs $0.59); adjusted EPS of $0.83 beat the $0.73 estimate.
Estimated remaining collections reached $3.61bn, up 23%; the Bluestem portfolio bought in late 2025 added $32.2m of collections and $13.4m of revenue.
Operating costs rose 23% to $98.4m, mainly court costs and agency and legal commissions; the cash efficiency ratio was 72.9% vs 72.2%.

Leverage rose to 1.73x from 1.59x as borrowing funded purchases; $300m of notes were repaid from the credit line and $100m of 2030 notes added. Dividend of $0.24 declared; $58.9m of shares bought back this year.

guidance.summary: Jefferson Capital gives no financial outlook. It had $384.3m of committed forward-flow purchase agreements at 30 September.

watch: Whether purchase volumes stay this high and how forward-flow commitments develop.
